alternatives: A lazy self-loop clock would change rates without changing support. Not used.
description: Every permitted pair toggles with weight 1 in every state.
expressive: Already the laboratory baseline. No new mechanism.
feasibility: Exact through N=6 on a complete carrier. N>=7 exhaustive kernels are out of budget.
formulation: Current-state weight table, constant 1. CL bookkeeping J=0, max K=0.
methods: Exact weight table and recurrent classes.
phenomena: The control against which a constraint is compared.
title: Neutral single-toggle baseline

alternatives: The same zero written as a long conjunction is a different expression of the same support.
description: The toggle of a declared pair has weight 0 when another declared pair is present, or when it is absent.
expressive: Current-state weight. One literal. Not a new event.
feasibility: Exact on carriers with at most 10 bits in the first batches.
formulation: One predicate, effect prohibit, action either. Support shrinks. Existing prohibit, not CL-T12.
methods: Exact support count and recurrent classes.
phenomena: Change of transition support, possible new deadlocks.
title: Hard prohibit on one literal

alternatives: A global rescaling of every weight leaves the chain unchanged. A state-dependent factor does not.
description: The toggle weight of a declared pair is multiplied by an integer greater than 1 when a literal holds.
expressive: One positive feature, K=2, J increased by 1. Cost is one literal, not a new axis.
feasibility: Same bound as the baseline.
formulation: Effect multiply, factor an integer >= 2, action either. Strictly positive if no prohibit is present. Inside CL-T12.
methods: Weight hash and, when the stationary law is unique, occupation.
phenomena: Relative rates change while support stays full.
title: Positive multiply on one literal

alternatives: An integer divisor when the literal holds is a different syntax for a related table. Not in the opening composer.
description: Multiplying when a literal is absent raises the weight off the literal and leaves the weight on the literal at baseline.
expressive: Same feature type. Polarity is which literal.
feasibility: Same bound as IDEA-C02.
formulation: Same multiply effect with polarity absent. Not a second mathematical effect.
methods: Paired cells that differ only in polarity.
phenomena: Whether polarity is a real contrast or a relabeling of favour.
title: Disfavour as the opposite polarity

alternatives: Encoding direction as two named events would be a different clock.
description: A constraint applies only when the affected pair is absent (formation) or only when it is present (dissolution).
expressive: Still one current-state weight. K rises by the extra literal. Not history.
feasibility: Exact on the same carriers. Stationary iteration is the fallback.
formulation: Action form or dissolve adds the pair's own bit as a literal. The weight then depends on the bit being toggled.
methods: Recurrent classes and a stationary solve only when the law is unique.
phenomena: Direction-specific support. The balance shortcut pi proportional to total weight need not apply.
title: Conditional formation and conditional dissolution

alternatives: A composer in which later constraints overwrite earlier ones would make order part of the law. That composer is not the opening one.
description: Two or more elementary constraints name the same toggle.
expressive: J counts features. max K stays the K of the richest single feature, not the sum of features.
feasibility: Ablation is one extra compile per constraint.
formulation: Opening composer: any matching prohibit sets the weight to 0; otherwise the baseline is multiplied by every matching factor. Order does not matter for these two effects.
methods: Ablation: effective cardinality is how many constraints change the table when removed.
phenomena: Reinforcement, redundancy, and a prohibit that voids a multiply on the same region.
title: Several constraints on one event

alternatives: Normalisation can couple events even when the integer weights factor. That coupling is a clock effect and must be labelled as one.
description: Constraints name different toggles.
expressive: Sum of the separate features. Still current state.
feasibility: Same bound.
formulation: Same composer, disjoint event indices.
methods: Weight hash against the single-constraint cells, plus recurrent classes.
phenomena: Whether the joint chain differs from the overlay of the separate supports and rates.
title: Several constraints on different events

alternatives: Syntactic identity of source text is a weaker equivalence than weight-table identity.
description: Count constraints written down, constraints whose removal changes the table, constraints active in a state, and constraints that touch one event.
expressive: Bookkeeping on top of the weight table.
feasibility: Cheap beside the compile.
formulation: Four integers, computed, not inferred from the prose.
methods: Ablation and a per-state active count.
phenomena: A long list can leave the baseline table. A short list can make the support state-dependent.
title: Declared cardinality against effective cardinality

alternatives: Leaving the count as one token would blur K. The atlas must not do that.
description: A weight depends on how many neighbours or incident pairs are present, not on one named literal.
expressive: Current state if the count is a function of current bits. Not opened in the first grammar.
feasibility: The expansion is exact and can be large. Not in atlas-001.
formulation: A count is a compound feature. CL: the formal K hierarchy is literal-only. Expanding a count is a disjunction whose J grows.
methods: Compile the expansion and hash it against a literal list, when a round chooses it.
phenomena: Whether a count creates behaviour a short literal list does not.
title: Local count predicates

alternatives: Putting the needed bit into the current state is the gate's trade-off, when the bit is present.
description: The next weight depends on which path reached the current graph.
expressive: Not in the opening grammar. A form/dissolve rule is still current state, because it reads the current bit.
feasibility: Open. A one-step memory on 10 bits doubles nothing small enough to ignore.
formulation: Two histories, same current bits, different next rows. The compilation gate says no increase of K or J at unchanged current state represents that.
methods: Only after a witness. The state would grow by a history coordinate.
phenomena: Memory beyond the current relation set.
title: Explicit history

alternatives: A complete graph with a prohibit that freezes some pairs forever is a different chain: those pairs still have bits.
description: Only a listed set of pairs are events. Other pairs do not have bits.
expressive: Fewer current bits. Not a geometry.
feasibility: A five-node chain has 4 bits and 16 states. Easy.
formulation: State space 2^(|carrier|), not 2^(N choose 2). The carrier is an instrument, declared in the spec.
methods: Same common core. Do not embed the chain as a complete graph with frozen absent pairs unless that different model is the cell.
phenomena: How the same constraint text behaves when the permitted pairs change.
title: Sparse permitted carrier

alternatives: A path index on the complete graph groups symmetry orbits. It is not this carrier.
description: Consecutive pairs only: (0,1), (1,2), ... .
expressive: Same grammar on a smaller bit set.
feasibility: Exact for short chains.
formulation: Listed carrier. Path length is the number of permitted edges. Six edges would be seven nodes and is not a target.
methods: Common core. Compare with the complete carrier only as a contrast of state spaces.
phenomena: Effects along a succession of permitted relations, as distinct from transmission inferred from a path index on a complete graph.
title: Chain carrier

alternatives: Calling a cycle an emergent rhythm would confuse the instrument with the chain.
description: A star of permitted pairs, or a cycle of permitted pairs.
expressive: Same grammar.
feasibility: A 4-cycle has 16 states. A 3-star has 8.
formulation: Listed carriers. The cycle is an imposed dependency loop in the carrier, not an observed oscillation.
methods: Common core on small listed carriers.
phenomena: Whether carrier shape changes support, recurrence, or occupation under the same constraint types.
title: Branch and cycle carriers

alternatives: A complete graph with a constraint that happens not to mention some edges is coupled by normalisation.
description: Two or more components in the permitted graph.
expressive: Same grammar. The product structure, if present, is a theorem to check, not an assumption.
feasibility: Very small.
formulation: Listed edges with no path between some nodes. Component count of the carrier is an instrument field.
methods: Weight hash and per-edge occupation when unique.
phenomena: Whether constraints that only see one component leave the other at baseline.
title: Disconnected carrier

alternatives: Imposing the pathway and then reporting it as propagation is the artefact this idea exists to avoid.
description: Study a constraint on one link of a chain and the occupation of later links.
expressive: No new state.
feasibility: Open after carriers exist.
formulation: Requires IDEA-R02. Depth is graph distance on the carrier, declared as an instrument.
methods: Not the RRC-001 path index.
phenomena: A difference that is flat along the chain is an orbit or a clock effect until a contrast shows otherwise.
title: Consecutive permitted relations

alternatives: A single nested Boolean expression with the same truth table is an equivalence, not a new branch.
description: One literal affects several events, or several literals affect one event.
expressive: Current state.
feasibility: Fits the opening composer.
formulation: IDEA-C05 and IDEA-C06. Branching of the rule text is not branching of a carrier.
methods: Keep the two coordinates in separate fields.
phenomena: Rule-dependency shape versus carrier shape.
title: Branching conditionality

alternatives: The period-2 parity of any single-toggle chain is a clock fact and is not evidence of a cyclic rule.
description: Constraints whose conditions form a cycle on the carrier edges.
expressive: Current state if each condition is a current bit.
feasibility: Open. Easy at N=3 already, where three pairs can cycle.
formulation: A cycle in the rule-dependency graph. Distinct from a cycle carrier and from a periodic Markov chain.
methods: Record the dependency cycle as syntax. Record period only if the transition graph has it.
phenomena: Feedback in the rule text. Oscillation is something the chain might show, not something the rule is asked to show.
title: Cyclic relational dependence

alternatives: Calling the subset a new node would add a state the dynamics have not earned.
description: Pairs that run between two named node sets, with the insides hidden or kept.
expressive: Projection of the current state.
feasibility: Open. N=4 is small. Not scheduled in the first batch.
formulation: RRC-001 used one such cut for lumpability. The atlas has not repeated it. A collection is designated, not discovered.
methods: Strong lumpability only when a round freezes that observable. Not the default core.
phenomena: Interface laws under elementary constraints rather than under wedge families.
title: Relations between designated collections

alternatives: Naming the same literal a higher-order relation would duplicate an existing mechanism.
description: An existing pair is the condition of another pair's weight.
expressive: Pair-to-pair literals compile. Independent hyperedges do not.
feasibility: The compiling case is the opening grammar. The hyperedge case is open and not feasible inside it.
formulation: This is IDEA-C01 and IDEA-C02. It does not yet require a hyperedge. An independent hyperedge, not a function of pair bits, would fail the opening gate.
methods: Record the compilation. Do not add a hyperedge in the first grammar.
phenomena: Whether 'relations on relations' is already pair-to-pair conditionality.
title: A relationship as a participant in a further constraint

alternatives: RRC-001's two-triangle cut is one designated projection, already reported, not a template to extend by default.
description: A structure used as a constituent of a larger structure, under more than one definition.
expressive: Depends on the definition. May be a projection, a product of carriers, or a new coordinate.
feasibility: Open. Not in the first batch.
formulation: Definitions differ: designated subsets, interfaces, carriers of carriers. None is assumed to preserve the grammar or to have an exact interface.
methods: Idea library first. One small frozen example only after the elementary atlas has a baseline.
phenomena: What, if anything, is stable across one composition step.
title: Recursive composition

alternatives: Narrating the rule chain as the behaviour of the chain.
description: A chain of conditions in the rule text is not a cascade in the dynamics.
expressive: Bookkeeping.
feasibility: Can be computed from the constraint list with no extra states.
formulation: Store the length of the longest condition chain in the spec. Store dynamical reach separately.
methods: Two fields. No summary that adds them.
phenomena: Keeps the instrument out of the observation column.
title: Imposed rule cascades versus observed cascades

alternatives: A single nested hierarchy is one option on this list, not the default.
description: Two groupings of the same carrier that are not nested.
expressive: Unknown until a definition is chosen. Do not force it into the subset language if that changes the meaning.
feasibility: Not scheduled. Kept because feasibility is not an entry condition.
formulation: Not one tree. A later round would have to name the groupings as instruments.
methods: None in the engine yet. Library only.
phenomena: Whether observations depend on which grouping is written down.
title: Overlapping and non-hierarchical descriptions

alternatives: Treating a longer list as automatically more organised. The atlas does not do that.
description: Declared lists longer than the three-constraint cells already run. Candidate lengths include 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10.
expressive: The opening composer. Declared J is the list length. Expansion J of a compound predicate is a different number.
feasibility: Exact ablation at or below 16 constraints. Exhaustive enumeration of every list is not the proposal.
formulation: Same prohibit-then-product rule. Effective cardinality and kernel-effective cardinality stay separate from the declared length.
methods: Weight hash, kernel fingerprint once it exists, ablation under the 16-constraint cap.
phenomena: Long lists whose table is short, and short lists whose support is state-dependent.
title: Higher declared cardinality

alternatives: A real-valued rate is a different clock and is not this alphabet.
description: Multiply factors other than 4, drawn from the integers of at least 2.
expressive: The opening composer already accepts any such integer.
feasibility: Same state spaces as the factor-4 cells.
formulation: Atlas-001 and atlas-002 used factor 4 only. That was a choice of cells, not a limit of the grammar.
methods: Paired cells that differ only in the factor.
phenomena: Whether strength changes support, the kernel, or only the raw integers.
title: Weight alphabet beyond four

alternatives: Calling two scaled tables equivalent under a continuous-time rate clock. That clock is not halt_self_loop.
description: A change of integer weights that leaves every discrete-time transition probability the same.
expressive: Bookkeeping on a current-state table. Not a new event.
feasibility: Exact once rows are reduced by their gcd. Zero rows stay zero.
formulation: P(e|x) = w(e,x) / sum_f w(f,x) when the row sum is positive. A zero row is the halt self-loop. Dividing a positive row by gcd(row) is an exact fingerprint for this clock only.
methods: Separate removal counts for the raw table and for the reduced rows.
phenomena: A constraint that changes the integers and does not change the normalised kernel.
title: Raw change with an unchanged kernel

alternatives: Hash equality after an undeclared reordering of edges. That is not this type.
description: Two specifications have the same integer weight table in the same declared edge order.
expressive: The existing sha256 of the canonical JSON table.
feasibility: Already computed for atlas-001 and atlas-002.
formulation: EQ-004 through EQ-007 are this type. Those rows predate the type field.
methods: weight_sha256.
phenomena: Identity of tables, including cases where the declarations differ.
title: Weight-table equivalence

alternatives: Floating-point comparison of rows. Exact equivalence does not use a tolerance.
description: Two tables induce the same halt_self_loop transition probabilities, possibly after a declared state mapping.
expressive: No new state. A fingerprint of the tables.
feasibility: kernel_sha256 is stored on every atlas-003 and atlas-004 result. Row gcd stays cheap beside the compile. No two of those cells share a kernel without sharing the integer table.
formulation: Positive rows are divided by their gcd. A zero row stays the zero row. Different shapes are not compared unless a mapping is declared.
methods: Integer reduction, then the same canonical hash as the weight table.
phenomena: Distinct raw tables with one discrete-time kernel. The only catalogued case is EQ-008, a method identity.
title: Normalised kernel equivalence

alternatives: Assuming every rule is covariant because the composer does not mention coordinates.
description: Equivalence under a declared permutation of node labels, of carrier-edge order, or under a named graph isomorphism.
expressive: A mapping stored with the comparison. The hash function itself does not search permutations.
feasibility: Small carriers can be checked exactly. A search over all N! labelings is not the default.
formulation: The mapping is part of the claim. Hash equality in unrelated orders is not relabelling equivalence.
methods: Push the permutation through the carrier and the rule, then compare tables or kernels.
phenomena: Where a label-free template is covariant, and where a designated label is an instrument.
title: Relabelling equivalence

alternatives: Reading only the second listed edge, which is the atlas-002 placement instrument.
description: The weight of an event depends on whether any currently present carrier edge shares an endpoint with that event.
expressive: Current-state single-toggle weights. The condition is a disjunction over the incident carrier edges. CL-T12 covers a strictly positive case by growing J and K. A zero remains prohibit. A count of those edges is a compound feature and is not this Boolean predicate. Not a new primitive.
feasibility: Exact on the four-edge carriers already used.
formulation: Neighbourhood: every other carrier edge that shares a node with the event. Evaluated on the current presence bits. A static fact that two named edges share a vertex does not by itself make the dynamics depend on topology.
methods: Compare with a designated-bit rule on chain and branch. Record the conjunction-expansion cost separately from declared J.
phenomena: Carriers that the bit grammar did not separate.
title: Incident-neighbour predicate

alternatives: Using that static bit as if it were a state-dependent neighbourhood.
description: Two designated edges either share an endpoint or they do not. That fact does not change from state to state.
expressive: A property of the carrier listing. Not a weight.
feasibility: Readable from the edge list.
formulation: If the rule then always consults one of those edges, the dynamics are still a designated-bit rule.
methods: Keep static incidence out of the predicate column unless the truth value depends on the current state.
phenomena: A representation that looks topological and computes the same table as a bit index.
title: Static incidence is not a dynamical predicate

alternatives: A rule that names node 0, or the first listed edge. That is an instrument and is not claimed to be covariant.
description: One predicate applied at every carrier edge, rather than at one labelled edge.
expressive: The same predicate, copied by the carrier. The copy is explicit in the constraint list.
feasibility: One constraint per edge on the small carriers.
formulation: A node permutation pushed through the carrier and through every event should preserve the table in the image edge order, when no label is designated.
methods: Independent permutation checks. They are validation when they are identities of the compiler, and cells only when a plan freezes them.
phenomena: Covariance, and the labelled rules that break it.
title: Label-covariant templates

alternatives: Sorting degrees by node label. That sequence depends on the names. The non-increasing sequence does not.
description: The non-increasing degree sequence of the graph that is present, isolated nodes included.
expressive: A function of the carrier geometry and the current bits. Not a function of the weight table.
feasibility: Cheap at the state counts already compiled. ATLAS-Q07 asks whether a later core carries it and does not schedule that core.
formulation: On the atlas-002 chain and branch, component counts agree on all 8 masks and these sequences differ on masks 5 and 7.
methods: Hash the sequences in state order when a core includes them. Do not rewrite atlas-002 results to insert them.
phenomena: Two carriers with one weight table and different present graphs.
title: Present degree sequence

alternatives: Reading the length of the rule chain as a measured propagation depth.
description: Imposed condition chains of more than one step, kept as syntax.
expressive: The dependency graph already stored. No new state.
feasibility: Exact while the dependency graph has at most 12 edges involved.
formulation: Vary the length of the imposed path as a coverage coordinate. Store it apart from reachability of the Markov chain.
methods: The existing imposed_rule_dependency field. Not a hop observable of the occupation.
phenomena: Different syntax lengths with ordinary dynamics, and the converse.
title: Condition chains of several lengths

alternatives: Reporting an approximate lumping as an exact interface.
description: An effective description that is allowed to be approximate, with the distance declared.
expressive: A projection plus a numerical or exact defect. Not a new event.
feasibility: Open. Not a default core field. RRC-001 already computed exact lumpability defects for other rules.
formulation: The defect, the partition, and the clock are part of the definition. No cell is implied.
methods: Only if a later plan names the partition and the defect. Strong lumpability remains the exact case.
phenomena: Small defects, large defects, and projections that are not Markov.
title: Approximate effective descriptions

alternatives: Assuming the interface chain uses the same prohibit-and-multiply grammar.
description: A composition step that might preserve the form of the transition law, transform the weights, or lose a closed description.
expressive: Unknown until the composition map is defined. The compilation gate still applies.
feasibility: Open. Several inequivalent definitions. No one of them is the default.
formulation: Separate rows for: exact preservation, transformed weights on the same event shape, and failure of a closed description. None is a prediction.
methods: Idea library. A cell requires one named map.
phenomena: What a named composition does to support and to weights.
title: Composition that preserves, transforms, or loses a description

alternatives: Forcing an overlap into a tree so that the current subset language can store it.
description: Groupings of one carrier that share nodes or edges and are not nested.
expressive: Not chosen. A subset language would change the meaning if the overlap is not a subset relation.
feasibility: Not scheduled. Kept because feasibility is not an entry condition.
formulation: The groupings would be instruments. IDEA-L08 names the same territory; this row adds the refusal to encode an overlap as a tree.
methods: None in the engine.
phenomena: Dependence on which overlapping cover is written down.
title: Overlapping covers that are not trees

alternatives: Treating every recurrent class, or every grammar, as a dominating set.
description: Deadlocks of one uniform incident prohibit are the total dominating sets of the carrier line graph.
expressive: The existing incident-neighbour prohibit. Not a new primitive.
feasibility: Exact enumeration on the small carriers already compiled. Checked by tests/test_domination.py.
formulation: docs/line-graph-domination.md. EQ-014. The identity stops when the template, polarity, or action changes.
methods: Independent set enumeration against compile_weight_table. Stored atlas-004 counts compared, not recomputed as a round.
phenomena: Absorbing states of this one rule. The chain has additional recurrent classes.
title: Line-graph total domination for one prohibit
